idiom_name: frozen contract component + bi-directional translator + explicit rejection path
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: one component per legacy contract that holds (1) the contract itself - signatures, formats, names, defaults and error codes copied from the legacy interface and treated as unmodifiable - (2) a translator mapping inbound legacy payloads to canonical commands and canonical results back to legacy payloads, and (3) a rejection path (legacy-equivalent error, or a dead-letter destination when the boundary is asynchronous) for anything the mapping cannot represent. Route the old shape to the window explicitly - its own channel, route or version prefix - so retiring the window is a routing change rather than code archaeology. Pin the contract with golden conversations before writing the translator, and give the window an owner and a review or expiry date, because a frozen contract nobody retires is the next legacy system.
code_sketch:
legacy_route(old_payload) -> window:
    cmd    = translate_inbound(old_payload)   # total mapping, defaults named explicitly
    result = core.handle(cmd)                 # canonical model, unaware of the old shape
    emit(translate_outbound(result))          # exact old shape, incl. error semantics
  on unmappable(old_payload):
    reply_with_legacy_error(old_payload)      # or dead-letter when asynchronous
pitfalls: Letting the legacy shape leak inward: once the core consumes legacy DTOs, the window has failed and the core has become the new legacy system.
Passing opaque payloads through ('just forward the blob'): nothing is translated, so the old semantics survive unexamined and the new contract is never really in force.
Mapping only the happy path: absent fields, unknown codes and error replies are exactly where legacy clients break.
